title: Hollow and Salt
premise: Beatrix Thackeray has spent her life guarding the Hollow Gate, the last sealed crossing between the human realm and the drowned kingdom of Saltmere, whose exiled king once swore a covenant of separation to end a devastating war. When a century-old prophecy book names tonight's date and her own name, Beatrix discovers the covenant is failing: the gate is reopening, and only a Thackeray — descended from the gate's original forger — can reforge it by surrendering her memories of everyone she loves. Guided by a smuggler who turns out to be Saltmere's lost prince in exile, she journeys through Thornfell's hidden roads to the covenant's broken anchor-stone. In the climax she refuses the old bargain, instead binding the covenant to shared memory rather than sacrifice, opening a controlled passage that ends both realms' isolation — though it costs her the keeper's role and forces her to build a new identity beyond the gate.
about_author: Wendell Thackeray is the pen name of a former lighthouse keeper turned novelist who writes fantasy steeped in borders, tides, and the people who guard them. Hollow and Salt is his third novel and the first set in the Thornfell mountains.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't Supposed to Exist
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. During a routine patrol of the Hollow Gate, Beatrix finds a prophecy book in a smuggler's abandoned cache that describes tonight's date, her name, and the gate's failure in detail written a century ago. A tremor splits the gate's seal before dawn. The emotional beat is dread hardening into resolve as she realizes her inheritance is a countdown.

chapters.title: Roads Only Smugglers Know
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, with smuggler Corren Vale guiding her through Thornfell's hidden passes toward the covenant's anchor-stone. He knows too much about Saltmere, and she catches him speaking its drowned tongue. Midpoint revelation: Corren is the exiled prince, alive because his mother broke the covenant to save him. The emotional beat is wary trust deepening into complicity.

chapters.title: What the Anchor Demands
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV at the sunken anchor-stone beneath Thornfell's highest tarn. The stone offers the old terms: reforge the covenant by erasing every memory she holds of love. Corren urges her to pay it; his kingdom starves behind the seal. Climax: Beatrix refuses, and instead cuts her palm on the stone to bind the covenant to exchanged memory — both realms will remember each other. The beat is defiance at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Keeper No Longer
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, weeks later. The gate now stands open under a new accord, tended jointly by humans and Saltmere's tide-priests, and Beatrix has no post, no title, and no duty. Corren offers her a place in his court; she chooses instead to map the roads between realms for ordinary travelers. Resolution beat: identity forged not by what she guards, but by what she connects.
